outcome.rationale: Combination therapy expected superior to botulinum toxin alone for spasticity (MAS, Tardieu) and ROM based on meta-analytic evidence. Six co-primary endpoints create multiplicity burden; small sample (n=20) may limit statistical significance for all endpoints. Trial likely demonstrates clinically meaningful benefits with at least 3-4 of 6 endpoints favoring combination, constituting overall success for adjunctive RESWT.

analysis_trace.finding: Single-center RCT comparing botulinum toxin plus RESWT versus botulinum toxin plus conventional therapy alone in pediatric cerebral palsy with lower extremity spasticity. N=20 estimated. Single-blind (assessor-blinded). Expected completion May 2025.

Children aged 2-18 years with spastic cerebral palsy receiving botulinum toxin injection for lower extremity spasticity. Exclusions include recent surgery, uncontrolled epilepsy, infection, coagulopathy. Representative of typical spastic CP population.

Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release reducing muscle overactivity. RESWT delivers mechanical pulses increasing nitric oxide, reducing alpha motor neuron excitability, and improving muscle mechanical properties. Combined therapy targets spasticity through complementary mechanisms.

Six co-primary endpoints covering spasticity (MAS, Modified Tardieu), function (Timed Up and Go), pain (FPS-R), ROM, and individualized goals (GAS). Measured at baseline, week 1, month 1, and month 3. All are clinically relevant for spasticity interventions.

Meta-analysis (Chang et al. 2023, PMID: 36832460) shows ESWT significantly reduces MAS scores versus control (sustained 1 month) and improves ROM (sustained 3+ months). Literature review (Khan et al. 2025, PMC12168712) confirms consistent MAS reductions, functional gains, and safety in 6 RCTs. Evidence supports additive benefit of combination therapy over botulinum toxin alone.

ESWT well-tolerated with no serious adverse events reported across pediatric CP studies. Botulinum toxin has established safety profile. Minor risks include transient pain, bruising. Favorable safety expected given non-invasive adjunct.

Primary risk is underpowering (n=20) to detect statistically significant between-group differences for all six endpoints. Heterogeneity in muscle groups injected may increase variance. Single-blind design may allow performance bias. Outcome timing (3 months) may miss sustained ROM benefits beyond MAS effects per meta-analysis.

No direct RCT results available for this specific trial (expected completion May 2025). Evidence relies on similar interventions in comparable populations. Exact treatment protocol (1500 pulses, 4Hz, 2 bar, 3 sessions) aligns with published effective parameters.
